Implement the PLL in Verilog, ensuring it can handle different frequency ranges and operates correctly in simulation.

module PLL (
    input wire clk_in,        // Input clock
    input wire reset,         // Reset signal
    output reg clk_out        // Output clock (8x)
);
    reg [2:0] phase_count;    // Phase counter
    reg clk_div;              // Divided clock for VCO

    // Phase Detector
    always @(posedge clk_in or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            phase_count <= 3'b000;
            clk_out <= 0;
        end else begin
            phase_count <= phase_count + 1;
            if (phase_count == 3'b111) begin
                clk_div <= ~clk_div; // Toggle VCO every 8 counts
            end
        end
    end

    // VCO output generation
    always @(posedge clk_div) begin
        clk_out <= ~clk_out; // Generate the output clock
    end
endmodule

The DMA controller should have a request input for each channel, a grant output for each channel, and a clock input to manage the sequential access. The controller should grant access to the first channel that requests it, using a round-robin method.

module dma_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire [3:0] req,    // Request lines from 4 channels
    output reg [3:0] grant   // Grant lines for 4 channels
);
    reg [1:0] current_channel; // To track which channel to grant next

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (req != 4'b0000) begin // If any request is active
            // Grant access to the first channel that is requested
            case (current_channel)
                2'b00: if (req[0]) begin grant <= 4'b0001; current_channel <= 2'b00; end
                        else if (req[1]) begin grant <= 4'b0010; current_channel <= 2'b01; end
                        else if (req[2]) begin grant <= 4'b0100; current_channel <= 2'b10; end
                        else if (req[3]) begin grant <= 4'b1000; current_channel <= 2'b11; end
                2'b01: if (req[1]) begin grant <= 4'b0010; current_channel <= 2'b01; end
                        else if (req[2]) begin grant <= 4'b0100; current_channel <= 2'b10; end
                        else if (req[3]) begin grant <= 4'b1000; current_channel <= 2'b11; end
                        else if (req[0]) begin grant <= 4'b0001; current_channel <= 2'b00; end
                2'b10: if (req[2]) begin grant <= 4'b0100; current_channel <= 2'b10; end
                        else if (req[3]) begin grant <= 4'b1000; current_channel <= 2'b11; end
                        else if (req[0]) begin grant <= 4'b0001; current_channel <= 2'b00; end
                        else if (req[1]) begin grant <= 4'b0010; current_channel <= 2'b01; end
                2'b11: if (req[3]) begin grant <= 4'b1000; current_channel <= 2'b11; end
                        else if (req[0]) begin grant <= 4'b0001; current_channel <= 2'b00; end
                        else if (req[1]) begin grant <= 4'b0010; current_channel <= 2'b01; end
                        else if (req[2]) begin grant <= 4'b0100; current_channel <= 2'b10; end
            endcase
        end else begin
            grant <= 4'b0000; // No requests, no grants
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Implement a simple Stop-and-Wait protocol in Verilog. The module will have input signals for data to be sent, a sender ready signal, and an acknowledgment (ACK) signal. The output will be the data sent and an indication if the sender is busy. The sender should wait for an ACK before sending the next data.
code:
module StopAndWait(
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    input sender_ready,
    input ack,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg busy
);
    reg state; // 0: idle, 1: sending

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            data_out <= 8'b0;
            busy <= 0;
            state <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // Idle state
                    if (sender_ready) begin
                        data_out <= data_in;
                        busy <= 1;
                        state <= 1; // Transition to sending
                    end
                end
                1: begin // Sending state
                    if (ack) begin
                        busy <= 0;
                        state <= 0; // Go back to idle
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

module crc_generator (
    input wire [31:0] data,
    input wire [31:0] polynomial,
    output reg [31:0] crc
);
    integer i;
    reg [31:0] data_reg;

    always @(*) begin
        data_reg = data; // Copy the input data
        crc = 32'b0; // Initialize CRC to zero

        for (i = 0; i < 32; i = i + 1) begin
            if (data_reg[31] == 1'b1) begin
                data_reg = data_reg ^ polynomial; // XOR with polynomial
            end
            data_reg = data_reg << 1; // Shift left
        end
        crc = data_reg; // Output the computed CRC
    end
endmodule

The module should store incoming samples until enough samples are collected to produce output samples at the lower rate.
code:
module sample_rate_converter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input enable,
    input [7:0] in_sample,
    output reg [7:0] out_sample,
    output reg out_valid
);
    reg [1:0] count;
    reg [7:0] sample_buffer [0:3]; // Buffer for 4 samples
    integer i;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            count <= 0;
            out_valid <= 0;
            out_sample <= 0;
            for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                sample_buffer[i] <= 0;
            end
        end else if (enable) begin
            sample_buffer[count] <= in_sample; // Store incoming sample
            count <= count + 1;
            if (count == 3) begin
                out_sample <= (sample_buffer[0] + sample_buffer[1] + sample_buffer[2] + sample_buffer[3]) >> 2; // Average the samples
                out_valid <= 1; // Signal that output is valid
                count <= 0; // Reset count for next set of samples
            end else begin
                out_valid <= 0; // Output not valid until enough samples are collected
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

    input [7:0] divisor,
    output reg [7:0] quotient,
    output reg remainder,
    input start,
    input clk,
    input reset
);

    reg [7:0] temp_divisor;
    reg [3:0] count;
    reg [8:0] result; // to hold remainder

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            quotient <= 8'b0;
            remainder <= 1'b0;
            count <= 4'b0;
        end else if (start) begin
            temp_dividend <= dividend;
            temp_divisor <= divisor;
            result <= {1'b0, temp_dividend}; // initialize result
            count <= 8; // 8 bits to process
            quotient <= 8'b0;
            remainder <= 1'b0;
        end else if (count > 0) begin
            result <= result << 1; // shift left
            result[0] <= temp_dividend[7]; // bring in next bit of dividend
            temp_dividend <= temp_dividend << 1; // shift dividend
            
            if (result[8:1] >= temp_divisor) begin
                result[8:1] <= result[8:1] - temp_divisor; // subtract divisor
                quotient <= {quotient[6:0], 1'b1}; // set quotient bit
            end else begin
                quotient <= {quotient[6:0], 1'b0}; // clear quotient bit
            end
            
            count <= count - 1; // decrement count
        end else begin
            remainder <= result[8:1]; // final remainder
        end
    end

    output reg cs,                // chip select
    output reg done               // done signal
);

    reg [7:0] data_out;           // data register
    reg sending;                  // flag to indicate sending process

        if (reset) begin
            mosi <= 0;
            sck <= 0;
            cs <= 1;               // chip select inactive
            done <= 0;
            bit_count <= 0;
            sending <= 0;

                cs <= 0;           // activate chip select
                data_out <= data_in;
                bit_count <= 8;    // start sending 8 bits
                sending <= 1;      
                done <= 0;         
            end
            
            if (sending) begin
                if (bit_count > 0) begin
                    sck <= ~sck;     // toggle clock
                    if (sck) begin
                        mosi <= data_out[bit_count-1]; // send bit
                    end else begin
                        data_out[bit_count-1] <= miso; // receive bit
                        bit_count <= bit_count - 1; // decrease count
                    end

                    cs <= 1;           // deactivate chip select

                end
            end
        end
    end

- y = C * x + D * u

A = [[0.5, 0.1], [0, 0.9]]
B = [[1], [0]]
C = [[1, 0]]
D = [[0]]

    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [1:0] x,        // Current state (2 bits)
    input [0:0] u,        // Input (1 bit)
    output reg [1:0] x_next, // Next state (2 bits)
    output reg [0:0] y      // Output (1 bit)
);
    
    // State-space matrices
    wire [1:0] A[0:1]; // A matrix
    wire [1:0] B[0:0]; // B matrix
    wire [0:0] C[0:1]; // C matrix
    wire [0:0] D[0:0]; // D matrix

    assign A[0] = 2'b01; // A[0][0] = 0.5, represent with 2'b01
    assign A[1] = 2'b10; // A[1][0] = 0.1, represent with 2'b10
    assign B[0] = 2'b01; // B[0][0] = 1, represent with 2'b01
    assign C[0] = 2'b01; // C[0][0] = 1, represent with 2'b01
    assign D[0] = 2'b00; // D[0][0] = 0, represent with 2'b00

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            x_next <= 2'b00; // Reset state
            y <= 1'b0;       // Reset output
        end else begin
            // State transition
            x_next[0] <= A[0][0] * x[0] + A[0][1] * x[1] + B[0][0] * u; // x_next[0]
            x_next[1] <= A[1][0] * x[0] + A[1][1] * x[1];               // x_next[1]

            // Output equation
            y <= C[0][0] * x[0] + D[0][0] * u;
        end
    end

module rsa_encrypt (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input start,
    input [127:0] plaintext,      // 128-bit plaintext
    input [127:0] n,              // 128-bit modulus
    input [127:0] e,              // 128-bit public exponent
    output reg [127:0] ciphertext, // 128-bit ciphertext
    output reg done
);

reg [127:0] temp;
reg [127:0] exp;
reg [127:0] base;
reg [3:0] state;

localparam IDLE = 0;
localparam LOAD = 1;
localparam CALC = 2;
localparam DONE = 3;

always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
    if (rst) begin
        state <= IDLE;
        ciphertext <= 0;
        done <= 0;
    end else begin
        case (state)
            IDLE: begin
                if (start) begin
                    base <= plaintext; // Load plaintext as base
                    exp <= e;         // Load exponent
                    temp <= 1;        // Start with temp = 1
                    state <= LOAD;
                    done <= 0;
                end
            end
            LOAD: begin
                if (exp != 0) begin
                    if (exp[0]) begin
                        temp <= (temp * base) % n; // Multiply temp by base mod n
                    end
                    base <= (base * base) % n;   // Square the base mod n
                    exp <= exp >> 1;              // Right shift exponent
                end else begin
                    ciphertext <= temp; // Store ciphertext
                    state <= DONE;
                end
            end
            DONE: begin
                done <= 1; // Indicate operation is complete
                state <= IDLE; // Go back to idle
            end
        endcase
    end
end

endmodule

The phase detector will take two inputs: a reference clock and a feedback clock. The output of the phase detector will control the VCO which generates the output clock. The loop filter will smooth the control signal sent to the VCO. The PLL should lock onto the reference clock and generate an output clock that is a multiple of the reference clock.
code:
module PLL (
    input wire clk_ref,        // Reference clock
    input wire clk_fb,         // Feedback clock
    input wire reset,          // Reset signal
    output reg clk_out         // Output clock
);

reg [1:0] phase_error;         // Phase error signal
reg [4:0] control_signal;      // Control signal for VCO
reg [4:0] vco_output;          // VCO output
reg [4:0] filter_output;       // Filter output

always @(posedge clk_ref or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        phase_error <= 2'b00;
    end else begin
        if (clk_ref == clk_fb) begin
            phase_error <= 2'b00; // No error
        end else if (clk_ref > clk_fb) begin
            phase_error <= 2'b01; // Reference is ahead
        end else begin
            phase_error <= 2'b10; // Feedback is ahead
        end
    end
end

always @(posedge clk_ref) begin
    case (phase_error)
        2'b00: control_signal <= control_signal; // No change
        2'b01: control_signal <= control_signal + 1; // Increase
        2'b10: control_signal <= control_signal - 1; // Decrease
    endcase
end

always @(posedge clk_ref) begin
    filter_output <= control_signal; // In a real PLL, you would implement a low-pass filter here
    vco_output <= filter_output; // VCO directly outputs the filtered signal for simplicity
    clk_out <= vco_output[0]; // Output clock is the least significant bit of the VCO output
end

endmodule

Design a 4-bit shift register with parallel load capability. The shift register should have a clock input, a parallel load enable input, and a 4-bit data input. When the load enable is high, the data input should be loaded into the shift register. When the load enable is low, the shift register should shift its contents to the right on each clock rising edge. The least significant bit (LSB) should be set to 0 during the shifting process.
code:
module shift_register (
    input wire clk,
    input wire load,
    input wire [3:0] data_in,
    output reg [3:0] data_out
);
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (load) begin
            data_out <= data_in; // Load data
        end else begin
            data_out <= {1'b0, data_out[3:1]}; // Shift right and set LSB to 0
        end
    end
endmodule

When writing, the data input should be stored in the memory cell, and when reading, the data output should reflect the stored value. The control signals will determine the operation (read or write).

    input wire we, // write enable
    input wire [15:0] din, // data input
    output reg [15:0] dout // data output
);

Design a D-latch in Verilog. The D-latch should have the following inputs and outputs:
- Input: D (data input), EN (enable signal)
- Output: Q (output that holds the value of D when EN is high)
The latch should hold its value when EN is low and should update its value based on D when EN is high.
code:
module D_latch (
    input wire D,
    input wire EN,
    output reg Q
);
    always @ (D or EN) begin
        if (EN) begin
            Q <= D;  // Update Q when EN is high
        end
        // When EN is low, Q holds its previous value
    end
endmodule

);

Design a dynamic range compressor that reduces the dynamic range of an input signal. The compressor should have an input signal of 8 bits and an output signal of 8 bits. Control the compression using a 2-bit control signal that determines the compression ratio. The compression ratios can be 1:1, 2:1, 4:1, and 8:1 based on the control signal values. The output should not exceed the maximum 8-bit value.
code:
module dynamic_range_compressor (
    input [7:0] in_signal,
    input [1:0] control,
    output reg [7:0] out_signal
);
    always @(*) begin
        case(control)
            2'b00: out_signal = in_signal;                            // 1:1 ratio
            2'b01: out_signal = in_signal >> 1;                      // 2:1 ratio
            2'b10: out_signal = in_signal >> 2;                      // 4:1 ratio
            2'b11: out_signal = in_signal >> 3;                      // 8:1 ratio
            default: out_signal = 8'b0;
        endcase
        // Ensure the output is capped at 8 bits
        if (out_signal > 8'hFF) out_signal = 8'hFF;
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple SD card interface controller in Verilog that handles read and write operations. Design a packet filtering module that checks incoming packets against a set of predefined rules to determine if they should be allowed or blocked. The input to the module is a 16-bit packet and the output is a single bit indicating whether the packet is allowed (1) or blocked (0). The filtering rules are as follows: 
1. Block packets with the source address 0xAAAA.
2. Allow packets with the destination address 0x1234.
3. Block packets with the protocol type 0x01 (e.g., ICMP).
4. Allow all other packets.

The input packet format is: 
- Bits 15-0: Packet data (assume that the first 4 bits represent source address, next 4 bits represent destination address, and the last 8 bits represent protocol type).
code:
module packet_filter (
    input [15:0] packet,
    output reg allow
);

    wire [3:0] src_addr = packet[15:12];
    wire [3:0] dst_addr = packet[11:8];
    wire [7:0] protocol = packet[7:0];

    always @(*) begin
        if (src_addr == 4'b1010) begin // 0xAAAA
            allow = 0; // Block
        end else if (dst_addr == 4'b0001) begin // 0x1234
            allow = 1; // Allow
        end else if (protocol == 8'b00000001) begin // Protocol type 0x01
            allow = 0; // Block
        end else begin
            allow = 1; // Allow all other packets
        end
    end

endmodule

Design a Verilog module that implements a simplified version of the A* search algorithm. The module should take in a current state, a goal state, and a heuristic value. Based on these inputs, it should output the next state to explore in an A* search. The inputs and outputs should be 5-bit wide to represent state values.
code:
module AStarAlgorithm (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [4:0] current_state,
    input [4:0] goal_state,
    input [4:0] heuristic_value,
    output reg [4:0] next_state
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            next_state <= 5'b00000;
        end else begin
            // Simplified A* logic: move towards the goal state
            if (current_state < goal_state) begin
                next_state <= current_state + 1; // Move up
            end else if (current_state > goal_state) begin
                next_state <= current_state - 1; // Move down
            end else begin
                next_state <= current_state; // Reached the goal
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

Create a Verilog module that implements a simple Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) controller. The controller has a clock input, a reset input, and a voltage level input. Based on the voltage level, the controller should adjust the frequency of an output clock signal. The frequency should be set to one of three levels based on the voltage input: 
- 1.0V → 200MHz 
- 0.9V → 150MHz
- 0.8V → 100MHz
If the reset input is high, the output frequency should default to 200MHz.
code:
module dvfs_controller(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [1:0] voltage_level, // 00: 1.0V, 01: 0.9V, 10: 0.8V
    output reg freq_out
);

reg [31:0] counter;
reg [31:0] freq_div;

always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        counter <= 0;
        freq_out <= 1; // Default to high frequency
        freq_div <= 5; // Default divisor for 200MHz
    end else begin
        case (voltage_level)
            2'b00: freq_div <= 5;   // 200MHz
            2'b01: freq_div <= 6;   // 150MHz
            2'b10: freq_div <= 10;  // 100MHz
            default: freq_div <= 5; // Default to 200MHz
        endcase
        
        counter <= counter + 1;
        if (counter >= freq_div) begin
            freq_out <= ~freq_out; // Toggle frequency output
            counter <= 0;
        end
    end
end

endmodule

description:
Create a Verilog module for a simplified sliding window protocol that manages the sending and receiving of data packets. The protocol should support a window size of 4 packets, with a sender and receiver that can acknowledge received packets. Implement the sender and receiver state machines with the following functionalities:
1. The sender can send packets when it is within the window size.
2. The sender can only send a packet when it receives an acknowledgment from the receiver for a previously sent packet.
3. The receiver can acknowledge packets it receives and can also indicate when it is ready to accept new packets.
The inputs to your module should include: 
- `clk` (clock signal),
- `reset` (active high reset),
- `send` (control signal to send a packet),
- `ack` (acknowledgment signal from the receiver).
The output should include:
- `data_out` (the packet being sent),
- `ready` (indicates if the receiver can accept more packets).
code:
module sliding_window_protocol(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input send,
    input ack,
    output reg [3:0] data_out,
    output reg ready
);
    reg [1:0] sender_state;
    reg [1:0] receiver_state;
    reg [1:0] window_base; // base of the window
    reg [1:0] next_packet; // next packet to be sent

    localparam IDLE = 2'b00,
               SENDING = 2'b01,
               WAITING_ACK = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            sender_state <= IDLE;
            window_base <= 0;
            next_packet <= 0;
            ready <= 1;
            data_out <= 4'b0000;
        end else begin
            case (sender_state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (send && ready) begin
                        data_out <= next_packet; // send the next packet
                        sender_state <= SENDING;
                        ready <= 0; // not ready until ack is received
                    end
                end
                SENDING: begin
                    sender_state <= WAITING_ACK; // wait for ack
                end
                WAITING_ACK: begin
                    if (ack) begin
                        window_base <= window_base + 1; // move window
                        next_packet <= next_packet + 1; // increment packet to send
                        ready <= 1; // ready to send next packet
                        sender_state <= IDLE; // go back to idle
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule
